tn_state_claim_verdict.claim: TN provides minimal transit funding - one of the worst states
tn_state_claim_verdict.verdict: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, REFRAMED: MATA's state $ is a flat ~$6.2-8.7M/yr FY22-25 (14.0% of its ops spend 2022-25) - not the smallest SHARE in the peer set (MO gives Bi-State just 1.1%; OH 2.1%), but those peers' totals ride on dedicated LOCAL streams that dwarf whole state grants. The structural finding: MATA levies $0 of its own taxes (NTD taxes_levied=0 every year) while COTA runs a dedicated agency-levied sales tax ($161.4M in 2024 alone - 3.1x MATA's ENTIRE 2024 budget); DDOT has a state+city dedicated mix and GRTC a state matching formula. NO dedicated state or regional funding stream exists for Memphis transit.

diagnosis.headline: Transit-share collapses to 0.5% because Memphis runs transit at one-fifth to one-half the per-resident money of every functioning peer AND because the money it does get is spent on a decade of financial-integrity failure and board churn instead of service. Funding is the binding constraint; governance failure + service-design retreat are the transmission mechanism; geography is a minor secondary effect.

evidence: NTD 2024 ops: Memphis $82/city-res vs Cincy $514, STL $1,041, Detroit $264 (5.7x-12.7x below Cincy/STL; 2.1-4.8x below Columbus/Indy/Richmond class)
farebox 4.9% and fares $2.5M = ~5% of budget (A5 2024-08-20: ~5%) - a rounding error, no self-funding
zero dedicated streams: NTD taxes_levied_by_agency = $0 every reported year vs COTA's $161.4M agency sales tax (2024)
city allocation flat $30M (FY25+FY26) despite a 2017 city-adopted plan calling for +$30M/yr that was never appropriated (MLK50 2026-11-24)

crisis mechanism: the 2024-25 'flat funding + more costs + fewer riders' formula (Mauldin, A5 2024-08-20) is literally a funding-deficit spiral: ops cut $85M -> $67M budget -> $53M NTD actual (2023) -> $52M (2024)
ranked_causes.falsifier: per-capita transit funding should NOT predict transit-share between these cities if geography or management dominated; it tracks (Cincy $514 -> 4-6.6% share; Memphis $82 -> 0.5-0.8%)

ranked_causes.cause: GOVERNANCE FAILURE (structure evidence) - the 2014-2024 decade of hidden deficit
evidence: MATA CFO to council: -$90M (2014), -$91M (2019) unrestricted net deficit, ten straight years, unreported (A5 2024-09-10)

TransPro diagnostic: no audit, gaps in contracts/projects/financial-commitment tracking, 'frivolous use of taxpayers dollars', boardings/rev-hr 23% below peer avg, cost/rev-hr 29% above (WREG 2024-10-11 + 2025-01-15)
board churn: full board replaced Oct 2024; 5 resign Sept 2025; trust replaces CEO Sept 2025; new board Sept 2026; 4 CEOs/interims in 30 months
trustee cost = state-class figure: $75,000/MONTH (MLK50 2026-11-24) for one interim leader
PwC: widespread missing financial documentation, unstructured budget process, grant-handling issues (MLK50 2025-09-05)
ranked_causes.falsifier: if money were the only problem, the FY26-27 funding-plateau years would show stability; instead trustee + board churn continue, which is what failure-of-institutions looks like when the dollar constraint is solved-but-not

evidence: 2017 Transit Vision promised +$30M/yr; never received; service fell from 320,000 annual hours (2017) to 215,000 (2026) - a one-third cut while peer cities grew (COTA VRH 820k->909k; GRTC 395k->444k, 2022-24)
Nov 2024: 23->18 routes, 60-min headways everywhere, Span 7pm/Sun 6pm (WREG 2024-09-24); 'current reduced schedule = 70% of COVID service schedule' (advocates, MLK50 2025-06-16)
'most routes: buses every 1-2 hours on weekdays' (Greer to council, WREG 2025-06-24); a case study rider took 6 hrs for a 3-mile grocery trip (WREG)

NATURAL EXPERIMENT: zero-fare policy (2025-11-16) lifted ridership +18-25% within weeks (WREG 2025-12-02, MLK50 2026-11-24: 2.7M trips, $4M rider savings, +20% year) WITHOUT adding a single bus route - proving suppressed demand exists when cost-barrier falls; but the supply side (VRH 693 weekday hrs 2025 vs 848 in 2022) caps the ceiling
ranked_causes.falsifier: the zero-fare +20-23% on a static network bounds the demand elasticity; it cannot reach 2-3% share on 693 weekday VRH

evidence: banked worker_ladder lane: Memphis mean commute 21.5/20.9/20.9/21.4 min (2021-2024) FLAT + ge45-share lowest of 6 cities = short commutes, not transit-served ones

this is the no-service-so-no-choice signature: with 693 weekday bus-VRH spread over 18 routes at 60-min headways, transit is not competitive, so everyone who CAN drive does; the city's ~6% no-vehicle households are structurally forced into rides/carpools
MATAplus denial of 300 paratransit trips/MONTH (Greer, WREG 2025-06-24) = even the legally-mandated floor is unmet
ranked_causes.falsifier: Houston (car-80%, similarly dispersed, mean commute 26-28min) runs 3-3.4% transit share on 3x Memphis per-resident funding - geography does not explain the 0.5%

diagnosis.tribe_frame: The founder's lens: a transit system is tribe-infrastructure - the daily shared ride that stitches the city into one labor market. Memphis's 0.5% means the tribe has no shared circulating commons; the bus is a residual charity for the no-vehicle poor, not a shared infrastructure input. The machine just counts it.

lever_tieback.target: move transit-share from 0.55% (ACS 2024) to 2-3% (peer-mid range; the bus-only exemplar class runs 2-4%)
honest_math_computed: 2% = 5,434 daily transit commuters vs 1,499 now = 3.6x; 3% = 8,151 = 5.4x (banked ACS 2024 city grain)
MATA productivity is not the problem (11.4 UPT/VRH vs GRTC 19.8, COTA 13.0) - the input is: 215,801 annual bus-VRH (2025)
at MATA's own $/VRH ($225, NTD 2024) 3.6x commuter base needs ~777,000 VRH = ~$175M/yr ops (vs $51.7M today = +$123M/yr)
at GRTC-class productivity ($173/VRH, 19.8 UPT/VRH) the same need = ~447,000 VRH = ~$77M/yr ops (+$25M/yr) - the productive-system floor

per-resident frame: taking MATA to the GRTC per-res level ($340/res) = $215M/yr (3.0-4.2x the Cincy-level); to IndyGo per-res ($155/res) = $98M/yr (+$73/res/yr - just ABOVE the banked $67-$69 per-resident class, i.e. ~1.1x the class)

dedicated-stream scale: COTA's 0.25% sales tax generated $161.4M in 2024 (Franklin County levy); Shelby County's narrower base implies a similar 0.5% levy class would be the right instrument class (a rate to be set by whoever designs the levy, not asserted here)
lever_tieback.years: COTA levy-to-Ride-time took 4-6 yrs (2018 levy -> lines 2018-2025); GRTC levy-to-Pulse took 2 yrs (2016->2018); realistic Memphis arc: yr-1 levy+board rebuild, yr-2 frequency floor (no route >30-min), yrs 3-5 BRT spine (mConnect $12M grant already awarded 2019, still unspent 2026) - holding 2%+ by year 5 is the honest timeline; MATA's own trustee targets trusteeship exit spring 2027 (Memphis Flyer 2026-11-10)

peer_class.why: legacy full-coverage network + massive local stream jump ($46.9M->$110.8M local 2023->2024, NTD) = 5-6.6% ACS share; farebox 21% - the high-funding regional model
the St. Louis City+County 0.1% sales taxes (2024 Measure to move money to STL City) + $254M local 2024 (NTD) = the money case; share 4.9-7.9%
state+city dedicated mix ($50.4M state + $105.4M local 2024) even amid a bus-availability crisis (1/3 of buses down per Detroit News 2024-08-06) - still 3.9-5.6% share

aspirational_bus_only_class.why_it_works: a permanent DEDICATED agency-levied 0.25%-class sales tax (levy 0.5% total incl county share; banked levy rate from 2024 election) funds a frequency-first bus redesign + BRT spines; the levy, not leadership, guarantees the money lands every year
aspirational_bus_only_class.lesson_for_memphis: MATA's $0 agency tax is the first structural fix; Shelby-county-scale dedicated levy >> annual council appropriation

aspirational_bus_only_class.why_it_works: the PULSE BRT spine (2018, the region's first) + the region's first bus-network redesign (2020) + strong state matching ($22-35M/yr) = highest productivity in the set (19.8 UPT/VRH) at MID funding - proof that frequency design converts dollars into riders better than raw size
aspirational_bus_only_class.lesson_for_memphis: share rose 2.5->4.2% two years after the redesign - the frequency+BRT arc pays in-mode-share within ~2 election cycles

aspirational_bus_only_class.why_it_works: the Marion County transit income tax (2016 voter-approved) tripled local funding; the Red Line bus-rapid-transit spine came online 2019 - closest analog to Memphis's mConnect ($12M federal, awarded 2019, stalled 2026)
aspirational_bus_only_class.lesson_for_memphis: the income-tax stream works mid-size; and a stalled BRT grant is recoverable - if IndyGo could turn a $75M 2017 federal share into 3 lines by 2025, mConnect's 7-yr stall is a governance choice, not a fate

exemplars.brt_european_frame: honored by pointer only per falsifier discipline: the honest floor for a US mid-size bus-only system = GRTC productivity 19.8 UPT/VRH at $340/city-res; European frequency-first systems imply lower $/rider again but require corridor densification Memphis lacks this session - not probed further
